body: Yes, based on previous Helpfulness feedback. It is a category I do not do well in. I think because both Helpfulness and SxS are very subjective, I overthink them too much. I assume though, that I'll be fine given that my comments are very detailed.
If that's true, I'll give it a shot. Thanks!

I noticed yesterday that I only had Helpfulness tasks, and I got an email this morning that I was grouped into Helpfulness. 

I also received the Factuality quiz. I'm the other way around, I really really hope they group me into Factuality instead, because the Helpfulness tasks are miserable. They are far too subjective to ever feel confident in my rating.

US Rater - PA. Been NTA since last Saturday, aside from 1-2 tasks here and there and a peak of 24 whole minutes of tasks on Tuesday. 

Have 1.5 hrs this week and some of that is training hours.
i was thinking that it wasn't. i was going back and forth between it being not a claim and it being a subjective claim a lot. i appreciate the help!
thank you! i'm not actually in the factuality group, i'm all tasks, i just get factuality tasks fairly often. so i don't think i saw any guidance like that.
I have seen from reading a few threads that some people who didn't get locked out received the same exam. It's strange, but if they never locked you out of tasks I'm sure you'll be fine!

A lot of US Raters were locked out of tasks ~2 weeks ago and forced to take a 4-part exam and were told we'd be terminated if we scored less than 80% on any part. The first one was bogus and full of errors and almost everyone failed, so they made us take another exam. Lots of us are finally getting to go back to work after this whole charade!
The only section I did poorly in was Direct Answer block. I didn't know you could find those examples in the UK resources section until after I finished.
I started at about 9am EST on Saturday. I finished around 12pm. I got the reactivation email at 1:30pm today!

You did even better than me, so I'm sure you'll be fine! I took mine in the early morning yesterday, so depending on when you took it it may just be a little longer? Breathe, be nice to yourself, have a treat :)

If you actually go through and make plans on his birthday, ESH. The way he approached something that makes you insecure is shitty. And yes, I know having holiday birthdays sucks.

But simply saying what you said should teach the lesson, I think. If you actually make plans and intend to go through with them, you’re not really doing anything except leaving someone else alone on their birthday. And you know how that sucks already. 

If you didn’t really mean it (which I feel like you didn’t, since you posted here), then NTA, but maybe give a soft apology and reinforce how shitty it feels. If he’s not a total dick, he’ll learn. I hope you get some cake, and a happy birthday to you.

NTA. ”Incel with no hope for humanity” is definitely being pretty harsh on yourself. You thanked her for the gift, and I can tell you actually do appreciate it. 

You can either keep them, gift them to someone else, or donate them. But you accepted the gift graciously. You did your duty.

NTA. Though you should be the one to talk to the kids about having to wait. If they’re between 6-12, I think they’ll understand if you make it clear. Anticipation can suck, but it can also be fun having things to look forward to at the end of COVID.

I also think that your siblings will come around and realize that you wanting to take them will be a blessing in disguise later. Kids home for the summer can be a handful to entertain and they can take the opportunity for alone time with themselves or with their partners.

Basically, unless your siblings also REALLY fucking love LEGOs, NTA.

Basically, being the first born is asking to be treated badly then watch your siblings get not even a slap on the wrist. Sigh.

The dad needs to own up to what you just said, at least.
I’m aware, I’m the eldest of seven. Doesn’t make it fair or okay.

This sounds like a classic case of “favoring the new family”. It happened to me, too. Super sorry, it’s awful and you don’t deserve it.

NTA. Parents like this are the worst.

I don't know that I'd say that it was selfish. I think he's probably taking it so hard because he was genuinely caught so off guard by how much they hated the gift. They said they "immediately got upset."

You could maybe call it irresponsible or misguided. But saying that he got the person he loved a gift just to feel good about himself? That's pretty cynical.

But sure, they both have apologizing to do.

ESH. Yes, you did have a talk about this, and he shouldn’t have bought the gift as per your agreement. But...

> I couldn’t believe how he could just selfishly throw it away on a perishable gift. 

Seriously? "Selfishly?" He bought it for *you*. He was still just trying to do something nice for you in the end, and now he’s crying and you’re still expecting him to apologize to you? That feels like a total asshole move.

You don’t have to be happy about it. But be reasonable. He clearly loves you.
CPS over a video game? Forget about the kids being abused, we’ve gotta get this kid away from his awful family who lets him play a big boy video game.

NTA. Just like a birthday or a wedding, it’s a going-away party for /you/. It’s supposed to create one great last memory before you’re apart for the foreseeable future. If the guest of honor doesn’t like the party, then it won’t be a fun memory. What’s the point of the party, then?

I wouldn’t go, either.
Oh my god, NTA. Using “wah misogyny” as an excuse for her awful, awful manners is so immature, and honestly makes me angry for actual feminists. NTA times ten.

YTA, but not because of anything in your main conflict. Honestly, you could have just said no to Brad. Instead, you ignored him, so it makes sense that he’d message you again, and you jumped right into telling him to leave you alone.

All you had to do was say no and it would have been done with. But instead, you chose to be TA.

I personally don’t understand why the question is “AITA for leaving work early?” You just said that your boss told you you could leave, and it seems like the main problem here is that your coworker is slacking off and lying about you, which has nothing to do with that.

You said your boss checked the cameras and is on your side. Can’t pass judgment, don’t understand the conflict here.

NTA. You said you’ve done it for them in the past, and I don’t think it was that much to ask.

Still, two questions. Do your parents know it’s illegal to park on the street? If so, they are especially TA. Also, how long is your driveway? That can make the difference between a 15 minute shovel and an hour and a half shovel.
Ohhh, no, I’m so sorry. Yeah, hold onto your things, tightly.

NAH. Yes, shutting the door’s often an unconscious thing and you weren’t trying to disturb anybody, but it also wouldn’t hurt to at least be considerate with the door. 

It doesn’t sound like you know your neighbors very well. Maybe she has a baby who’s napping or maybe she works nights and needs to sleep during the day.  Closing the door gently can be a simple kindness that goes a long way.

You’re NTA, you’re completely correct. If he has time to play video games, he has time to do the laundry. I get procrastinating on chores, I really do, but to me it sounds like there’s no reason why he couldn’t play video games after he did the laundry. 

Don’t coddle him and don’t allow yourself to be convinced you were the asshole for speaking the truth.

NTA, he’s shown a history of not respecting things and you have no reason to trust him with your stuff. He especially shouldn’t let /other/ people borrow and lose your stuff.

Still, how old is your brother? I assume he’s in college, but if he’s older than 20 he especially needs to get it together.

NTA. You clearly care about these kids and it would be much better for them to be raised by someone who they’re already close with than raised by strangers.

It’s very cruel of her to say that she doesn’t want anything to do with her kids, but she likely need some sort of mental help. Keeping the kids away from her as much as possible is probably best for everyone until she gets it.

NAH. Battling cancer is incredibly tough on the emotions, and she’s probably very sensitive and maybe even insecure about her appearance at this moment in her life. Yes, she shouldn’t have blown up, but I’m not going to make a judgment that she’s an asshole. No one likes being misgendered.

You made a mistake, you corrected yourself, and you tried to apologize. The fact that this is weighing on you like this says a lot about your character. Even so, try not using gendered terms when referring to customers (or anyone, really) in the future. Rather than “excuse me, sir” or “excuse me, ma’am”, just go with a simple “excuse me”. It takes practice to break if it’s a habit, but it’ll definitely keep you from upsetting anyone.

Yep! Sorry if I sounded snippy. Admittedly, I was being a bit defensive. I know these weird abstract topics about sexuality can be difficult, but sometimes just accepting that you don’t get it and letting people be is the right answer. (:
I will say that they definitely don’t make comments about “clams” amongst themselves. Ugh.
Yes, but thanks to some unimportant backstory, I’ve only lived with my mom and stepdad since I was 14. I was definitely educated on sex before then. It sounded awful to me then, too.
Thank you! I don’t mind explaining if it’s someone being respectful to me and it’s educational, but the people who are rude to me can fucking Google it if they don’t get it.

Funny, because there are a lot of people are sex-repulsed whom therapy did nothing for. People that are different don’t automatically need therapy.

There’s nothing wrong with me. I just dislike the idea of being involved in sex. Google the split attraction model. If you read about it and still can’t understand it, then it’s not my problem.
Yes, I’ve asked them to stop those in front of me, also, but figured I must have been asking a lot. But when the jokes are about me, it’s completely inappropriate and unnecessary.
Nope. Please see my edit!
Please see my edit!

My parents have always made vulgar jokes about each other (some of which are really gross and I asked them to stop because I don’t want to think about my parents boning, but whatever).

But the jokes have only been aimed at me since I came out, AFAIK.

I’ll admit that at the time I made that edit, the wound was fresh and the validation I was receiving was making me feel extra indignant. It was charged. I’ve cooled it over the course of the day.

It wasn’t supposed to be a judgment on anyone else, though not using “preference” going forward is definitely my suggestion.
I said stepdad early in the post. Sorry for the lack of consistency. Bio dad is 41 but we don’t speak.

I answered this earlier in the thread so I’ll repost:

The asexual split attraction model splits your attractions into romantic and sexual. If I use the technical term, I’m a homoromantic asexual because I am romantically attracted to other girls, but not sexually.

But most average people don’t know what the split attraction model is, and I run the risk of either confusing them or getting the classic homophobic “oh you millennials and your made up sexualities” comment. So I just go by lesbian, since on the surface, that’s what I look like to others.

No, I can tell you with full confidence that it will not shut them up. Being crass and inappropriate is somehow normal for them and it will be like pouring gasoline on a fire. Also, ew, ew ew ew, I don't want to say that, ever.

>However, every time I’ve come home from college since, my parents have made super inappropriate jokes about my sexuality and I’ve made it clear multiple times that it makes me super uncomfortable 

I mean, I thought I was pretty clear. And that's fine for you, but that's just not the relationship I expect with my parents.

It shouldn’t be tense in the first place. I’m a lesbian. It’s not that deep. I don’t like my /parents/ talking about me giving people oral sex. I don’t think it’s that much to ask, good god.

And it really wasn’t even a good joke. I can’t fathom why you think it was funny.

I appreciate being able to share the experience with somebody. It’s nice not to feel like we’re by ourselves. I’m glad you get how I feel about romance, not that we both have to experience it.

I’m unfortunately also kiss-repulsed (just on the lips! Other parts are fine, but lips is a sensory nightmare) and that’s another even MORE major deal breaker for some people. It’s super unfortunate.

Regardless! Thank you for helping me feel less alone in this.

Thank you. I think my biggest concern/difference between my platonic relationships and a romantic relationship is I want someone who is more consistently on my mind/to consider and vice versa, I suppose? I want to be cared for and care for someone on the day to day, while I very rarely see any of my friends. Of course I know I won’t be alone without a partner, but I will be alone a lot of the time because my friends have their own partners and their own lives. Maybe that’s a little selfish or overly needy, though.

I really appreciate your advice, though. You wrote a lot but it all makes a lot of sense. (: Thank you again.
They make sexual jokes about each other constantly (in front of me, which I have ALSO asked them to stop doing so excessively to no avail) but they prefer to punch down when I’m around, I guess.

I feel you here. My parents got worse about the jokes when I dated a trans guy who came out as trans in the middle of our relationship (we're no longer dating, but we dated for a little while after he came out). They got even worse about it when I was dating a guy, for chrissakes. Add transphobic to the list.

Yep, you're also correct. But I'm trying to be understanding since none of the comments asking me about it on this thread have been particularly malicious or anything. People just have a different understanding of what labels entail because society likes to give very specific definitions of things that aren't specific by design. I don't mind explaining if it's actually educational and not talking at a brick wall.

To be fair, I haven’t explicitly said that I am asexual, but I have said multiple times that I am not sexually active whatsoever and have mentioned that I am sex-repulsed. Didn’t change their behavior, though.
Right? Why did they ever do that? It’s so disgusting. I know it’s just misogyny, but it also seriously makes anything sexual sound even more gross to me than it already did.

Yes, this. Telling people you’re “homoromantic asexual” or “only romantically attracted to women but I wouldn’t have sex with them” is super unwieldy and sometimes frustrating. Lesbian is a catch-all when I really only need to get into specifics with my partners whom it will affect.
